data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A test constrains its subject rather than describes it when the test's failure path is causally upstream of the subject's accepted form \u2014 for example, when a mutation is installed under a shown-to-fail-first ritual and the failing installation becomes part of the subject's own guard structure.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the same mutation survives under a describe-only installation where the test is run after the subject is fixed, the constrain interpretation fails.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the 1/9 loss is explained by a simple coverage gap unrelated to installation order, the ritual mechanism is irrelevant.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If ordinarily-guarded modules lose 4/4 to 6/7 under the same shown-to-fail-first ritual, the specialness of compile.py disappears.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If a registry-size or author-specific confound explains the distribution, the constraint claim is weakened.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Shown-to-fail-first installation converts the test from an external measurement into an internal precondition: the subject is modified to expect and reject the failure mode before it is accepted. Under this installation ritual, the test no longer merely reports on a pre-existing object; it selects which object variant can exist. The 1/9 mutation lost in compile.py reflects a subject whose guard was keyed to declared data rather than added behaviour, so the test constrained only the declared surface.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
